records.title: Kaikōura lights
records.explanation: Explanations offered include Venus and Jupiter, squid-fishing boat lights, and meteors; none accounts for the radar returns to everyone’s satisfaction.
records.shape: Bright white lights with a red tinge; pulsing orb
records.witnesses: Safe Air crew, TV crew, Wellington radar
records.summary: After a Safe Air crew reported lights tracked by Wellington radar on 21 December, an Australian TV crew rode along on the Argosy newspaper run. On the night of 30–31 December they filmed lights pacing the aircraft off the Kaikōura coast in colour on 16 mm film, with Wellington controllers reporting matching radar returns.

timeline.text: Safe Air pilots report lights; Wellington radar has returns.
Argosy leaves Wellington with the TV crew.
Lights filmed off Kaikōura; radar contacts relayed.
Christchurch–Blenheim leg: orb tracks off the wing ~15 min.

records.title: Cecconi G.91R photographs over Treviso
records.explanation: The Italian Defence Ministry later said its photo interpreters had identified the object as a cylindrical balloon made of black plastic bags (a "solar balloon"). Cecconi rejected this, noting the object did not move in his jet's wake.
records.shape: Dull black, capsule-shaped, with a milky dome
records.witnesses: Maresciallo Giancarlo Cecconi; Istrana radar; Treviso tower
records.summary: Returning from a photo-reconnaissance sortie in a G.91R, Italian Air Force pilot Giancarlo Cecconi was asked to identify an object tracked by Istrana radar over Treviso air base. He found a dull black, capsule-shaped object about 6–8 m long at about 1,300 m. He made passes within about 100 m and took more than 80 photographs with the aircraft's reconnaissance cameras. Then radar and the tower both lost it.

timeline.text: Istrana radar reports an object over Treviso; Cecconi is vectored to it.
He photographs it with the nose camera, reverses and photographs again.
Radar and tower lose the object.
Defence Ministry: a balloon made of black plastic bags.

points.note: Over Treviso air base at ~1,300 m

records.title: Val Johnson — deputy's patrol car struck by a light
records.explanation: UFO researchers (Allan Hendry, Jerome Clark) consider it significant. Skeptic Philip Klass argued it was a hoax and that Johnson damaged the car himself. The patrol car is on display at the Marshall County museum.
records.shape: Beam of bright light just above the road
records.witnesses: 1 (Deputy Sheriff Val Johnson)
records.summary: Deputy Val Johnson was patrolling rural roads when he saw a bright light just above the road. It rushed toward his car, the car was engulfed in light, and he heard glass breaking. He said he was unconscious for 39 minutes. Deputies found the car skewed across the road. The windshield was cracked, a headlight and the roof light were broken, and an aerial was bent. Both his watch and the car's clock were 14 minutes slow. A doctor compared his eye irritation to "welder's burns".

timeline.text: Johnson sees a bright light near the road and drives toward it.
Light engulfs the car; glass breaks; he blacks out.
He radios for help; deputies find the car sideways on the road.
CUFOS and Honeywell engineers examine the car.

records.title: Dechmont Law — Robert Taylor
records.shape: Dome-shaped object; two spiked spheres
records.witnesses: 1 (forester Robert Taylor)
records.summary: Forestry worker Robert Taylor walked into a clearing on Dechmont Law and saw a large dome-shaped object hovering. He said two smaller spiked spheres rolled out, grabbed his trousers and dragged him toward it, and he passed out. He came to with torn trousers, grazes and a headache, and staggered home. Police recorded the case as an assault and found marks in the ground. It is often described as the only UFO event police have investigated as a crime. A marker now stands at the site.

timeline.text: Taylor enters the clearing and sees the object.
Spheres grab him; he blacks out.
He reaches home; the police are called.
Police find marks in the ground and open a criminal inquiry.

records.title: Manises — airliner diversion & Mirage intercept
records.explanation: Spanish Air Force files declassified in the 1990s did not confirm an anomalous object; researchers attribute the lights to refinery flare stacks and bright stars/planets.
records.shape: Red lights on a collision course; truncated cone
records.witnesses: TAE crew, 109 passengers, controllers, Mirage pilot
records.summary: TAE flight JK-297 from Salzburg (via Palma) to Las Palmas saw red lights approach on a collision course near Ibiza and track the aircraft after it changed altitude. The captain diverted to Valencia — the first airliner diverted by a UFO. A Mirage F1 from Los Llanos then chased lights that accelerated away.

timeline.text: Red lights close on the Supercaravelle near Ibiza.
Captain diverts to Manises; lights break off before landing.
Mirage F1 scrambled from Los Llanos, Albacete.
Pilot reports avionics interference near Sagunto; returns.

records.title: La Joya air base pursuit
records.place: La Joya air base, Arequipa, Peru
records.explanation: Peru’s air force kept the case quiet for decades; no explanation has been published. Peru has since set up an office (now DIFAA) for aerial anomalies, and U.S. documents on the case were later released.
records.shape: Large balloon-shaped object
records.witnesses: Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas; some 1,800 people at the base
records.summary: On the morning of April 11, 1980 about 1,800 people at the La Joya base saw a large, balloon-shaped object hanging still at around 500 metres. Lt Oscar Santa María Huertas, 23, took off in a Sukhoi Su-22 and fired 64 rounds at it without effect. He reported that it climbed away at up to 950 km/h, reaching about 19,200 metres, and stopped so suddenly that he had to swerve to avoid it. Peruvian army radar was said to show only his aircraft, while operators saw the object by eye. The engagement is said to have lasted 22 minutes, until his fuel ran low. The Peruvian Air Force kept the matter classified for decades; U.S. defence documents titled “UFO sighted in Peru” have since been released.

timeline.text: An object is seen hanging at ~500 m over the base; Su-22 pilot Santa María scrambles.
He fires 64 rounds; the object climbs away at up to 950 km/h.
Short of fuel, he breaks off; the object leaves.
U.S. documents on the case are released; Peru opens an aerial-anomalies office.

records.title: Todmorden — PC Alan Godfrey
records.shape: Diamond-shaped object hovering over the road
records.witnesses: PC Alan Godfrey; other officers saw a light that night
records.summary: Before dawn, PC Alan Godfrey was driving his patrol car along Burnley Road looking for missing cattle when he found a large, diamond-shaped object hovering about 5 ft above the road, blocking it. He sketched it from the car. The next thing he knew, he was farther down the road and some time had passed. He said the road surface under the object was dry though the rest was wet. Other officers reported a light in the sky that night. Later hypnosis sessions produced an abduction account.

timeline.text: Godfrey sees the object blocking the road and sketches it.
He finds himself farther down the road; about 15 minutes missing.
Regression hypnosis yields an abduction account.

records.title: Rendlesham Forest
records.place: Rendlesham Forest, outside RAF Woodbridge, Suffolk
records.explanation: The Ministry of Defence found no threat and did not investigate further. Skeptics attribute the lights to a fireball, the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees in the same direction) and bright stars.
records.shape: Metallic lit object in the forest; star-like lights
records.witnesses: USAF security police; Lt. Col. Charles Halt
records.summary: USAF security patrols at the east gate of RAF Woodbridge saw lights descend into the forest and went in to investigate. Two nights later deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a team that took radiation readings at three ground depressions and recorded his observations on a micro-cassette. His memo to the MoD is one of the most famous UFO documents in Britain.

timeline.text: Patrol sees lights descend into the forest.
Three depressions and marks on trees found; police called.
Halt’s team takes radiation readings; flashing red light to the east.
Halt memo sent to the Ministry of Defence.

records.title: Cash–Landrum incident
records.explanation: Army and Air Force inquiries found no helicopters or craft that matched; the witnesses’ lawsuit against the U.S. government was dismissed in 1986. Skeptics question the medical and helicopter claims.
records.shape: Diamond-shaped object venting flame; escorted by ~23 helicopters
records.witnesses: Betty Cash, Vickie & Colby Landrum; other motorists
records.summary: Driving home through the pine woods north-east of Houston, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum with her grandson said a blazing diamond-shaped object hovered over the road, radiating heat. As it rose, they counted about two dozen helicopters, many resembling CH-47 Chinooks. All three reported injuries afterwards, and they sued the U.S. government.

timeline.text: Light above the trees; object then hovers over the road ahead.
Object rises; helicopters close in around it.
Burns, hair loss and nausea reported.
Lawsuit dismissed: no evidence the craft belonged to the U.S. government.

records.title: Trans-en-Provence landing trace
records.explanation: The French government’s GEPAN (now GEIPAN, part of CNES) analysed soil and plant samples and reported heating and biochemical changes it could not attribute to a known cause. Skeptics suggest a vehicle or the witness.
records.shape: Lead-grey disc, two stacked saucers
records.witnesses: Renato Nicolaï
records.summary: Renato Nicolaï heard a whistle and saw an object land briefly on his terrace and fly off. The Gendarmerie took samples within a day; GEPAN’s laboratory analysis of the 2.4 m circular mark reported soil heated to 300–600 °C and chlorophyll changes in alfalfa leaves.

timeline.text: Object lands and departs almost immediately.
Gendarmes photograph and sample the ring-shaped trace.
GEPAN Technical Note 16 published.

records.title: Morenão stadium sighting
records.place: Estádio Morenão, Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
records.shape: Unidentified lights
records.witnesses: More than 24,000 spectators, players and the referee
records.summary: During a Brazilian championship match between Operário and Vasco da Gama, a crowd of more than 24,000 saw unidentified objects over the stadium. Players, including Cocada, and referee José de Assis Aragão described them. Among the spectators was Ademar José Gevaerd, who went on to become one of Brazil's best-known UFO researchers.

timeline.text: Objects seen over the stadium; play is interrupted.
Players and the referee describe what they saw to the press.

records.title: Hessdalen lights
records.explanation: Studied since 1983 by Project Hessdalen with an automated measurement station; hypotheses include combustion of dust from the valley’s ores, plasma, and piezoelectric effects.
records.shape: White, yellow or red floating lights
records.witnesses: Residents and scientists
records.summary: Lights have appeared over the 12-km Hessdalen valley since at least the early 1980s, peaking at up to 20 per week in 1981–84. Unusually, they have been measured: radar, spectra, magnetometers and a permanent camera station have recorded them, but their cause is still debated.

timeline.text: Peak activity; up to 20 sightings a week.
Project Hessdalen field campaign with radar and cameras.
Automated measurement station installed.

records.title: Hudson Valley "Westchester boomerang"
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: State police and the New York Power Authority attributed the sightings to pilots flying Cessna 152s in tight formation from Stormville Airport with coloured lights — a hoax the pilots reportedly enjoyed.
records.shape: V / boomerang of coloured lights
records.witnesses: Thousands across Westchester, Putnam, Dutchess and Fairfield counties
records.summary: For over a year residents of the Hudson Valley reported a silent boomerang or V of bright lights, sometimes "the size of a football field". Guards at the Indian Point nuclear plant reportedly saw it in June and July 1984, and a Brewster resident videotaped the lights on 24 July.

timeline.text: First wave of reports.
Claimed sightings over the Indian Point nuclear plant.
Bob Pozzuoli videotapes the lights in Brewster.

records.title: Dalnegorsk “Height 611” crash
records.explanation: Ball lightning and other plasma phenomena have been proposed. The reports of unusual metal fragments come mostly from the investigating group and have not been independently confirmed.
records.shape: Reddish sphere about 3 m across
records.witnesses: Residents of Dalnegorsk
records.summary: On the evening of January 29, 1986 residents of the mining town of Dalnegorsk saw a reddish, silent sphere about three metres across flying from the south-east at some 700–800 metres, at about 15 m/s. It crossed part of the town and came down on Izvestkovaya mountain, known as Height 611, burning on the slope. Investigators reported tiny metallic droplets 2–5 mm across, and fibres in a tangle of metal, quartz and gold-coloured threads. In Russia it is often called the best-documented UFO crash, although the technical findings come mainly from the group that investigated it.

timeline.text: A reddish sphere is seen crossing the town from the south-east.
It strikes Izvestkovaya mountain (Height 611) and burns.
A group led by Valeri Dvuzhilny collects droplets and fibres from the slope.

records.title: Brazil’s "Official UFO Night"
records.place: São José dos Campos – Rio de Janeiro – Goiás
records.explanation: The Air Force commander said "we have no explanation". The report declassified in 2009 described objects with speeds from hovering to supersonic and 90° turns.
records.shape: Red, white and green lights; 21 radar plots
records.witnesses: Controllers, F-5E and Mirage pilots, Embraer founder Ozires Silva
records.summary: Controllers at São José dos Campos and radar across south-east Brazil tracked about 21 unknown contacts. Embraer’s founder, flying in, saw red lights; the Air Force scrambled F-5Es from Santa Cruz and Mirage IIIs from Anápolis. Pilots reported lights that kept their distance and targets that appeared behind them.

Ozires Silva’s Xingu reports red lights near the coast.
F-5E JB17 airborne from Santa Cruz; follows a light to sea.
Mirage JG116 from Anápolis gets five radar contacts.

Air Force press conference with the pilots.

records.title: Torpo film
records.shape: Two bright objects, one flashing and throwing sparks
records.witnesses: A family and friends at a mountain farm
records.summary: A couple at a mountain farm near Torpo, with their son and friends, watched two bright objects in the evening sky, one moving dramatically, flashing and throwing off sparks. The husband filmed them. Ground Saucer Watch found no sign of a hoax, but said the apparent motion could come from camera shake and that the lack of reference points made the film inconclusive.

Film analysed by Ground Saucer Watch; no firm conclusion.

records.title: Japan Air Lines Flight 1628
records.explanation: The FAA’s radar returns were later dismissed as clutter / a split image; Philip Klass argued the crew saw Jupiter and Mars. The FAA found the crew professional and rational.
records.shape: Two small lights and a huge "mothership"
records.witnesses: Capt. Kenji Terauchi and crew
records.summary: A JAL Boeing 747 freighter on the Reykjavík–Anchorage leg reported three objects pacing it at 35,000 ft, including one Terauchi described as enormous. Anchorage controllers reported returns near the aircraft; the objects stayed with the plane through turns and descents until near Talkeetna.

timeline.text: Lights seen near the aircraft over eastern Alaska.
Crew reports to Anchorage ARTCC; traffic advisory.
Orbit and descent requested; lights stay with the jet.
Objects lost near Talkeetna; jet lands in Anchorage.

records.title: Gulf Breeze photographs
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: Considered a hoax. In 1990 the new owners of Ed Walters's former house found a styrofoam model UFO in the attic that a reporter used to reproduce the photos almost exactly. A local teenager also said he had helped fake them. Walters said the model was planted.
records.shape: Cylindrical craft with a ring of portholes and a glowing base
records.witnesses: Ed Walters; other residents later came forward
records.summary: Contractor Ed Walters gave the Gulf Breeze Sentinel five Polaroids of a glowing craft he said hovered near his home. Over six months he produced dozens more photos and video, and described being hit by a blue beam and seeing aliens. Researchers such as Bruce Maccabee backed the photos, and other residents reported sightings. After the model was found in 1990 and a reporter recreated the pictures, the case became a textbook example of a UFO photo hoax.

timeline.text: Walters takes the first Polaroids outside his home.
Many more photos and video; other residents report lights.
Styrofoam model found in the attic of Walters's former house.

records.title: Ilkley Moor photograph
records.explanation: Critics say the blurry photograph could show a person or a cardboard cutout, and ask why no picture of the craft was taken. Kodak experts found no sign of tampering, but the image is too grainy for firm conclusions, and the account changed under hypnosis.
records.shape: Small green humanoid; two-part silver craft
records.witnesses: Philip Spencer, a retired police officer (a pseudonym)
records.duration: Minutes; about two hours unaccounted for
records.summary: On the morning of December 1, 1987 Philip Spencer, a retired police officer, was walking across Ilkley Moor, between Ilkley and Keighley, when he said he met a small dark-green figure about 1.2 metres tall, with a large head and long thin arms. He took one photograph before it ran off, then saw a whitish, two-part craft rise from the moor with a loud hum. About two hours were missing from his journey, and his compass pointed the wrong way. A wildlife photographer said the figure matched no known animal and Kodak found no signs of tampering, but the US Navy optics specialist Bruce Maccabee called the image too grainy to test. Under hypnosis in March 1988 his story changed to one of being taken aboard and examined.

timeline.text: Spencer meets a small green figure on the moor and takes one photograph.
A whitish two-part craft rises from the moor with a loud humming sound.
He finds about two hours have passed, and that his compass points the wrong way.
Under regression hypnosis he recalls being taken aboard and examined.

UFOs at close sight — the Ilkley Moor encounter, 1987

records.title: Knowles family encounter
records.place: Nullarbor Plain, between Madura and Mundrabilla, Western Australia
records.explanation: No explanation has been established. The account rests on the four family members’ testimony and the physical details they described, and has been widely reported in Australia.
records.shape: Large glowing ball
records.witnesses: Faye Knowles and her sons Patrick, Sean and Wayne
records.summary: In the early hours of January 20, 1988, the Knowles family were driving across the Nullarbor Plain in their station wagon when a bright light appeared ahead. They said a large glowing object pursued the car for a long time and finally came down on the roof; the car seemed to be lifted off the road, and the engine and voices changed as if time were slowing. Mrs Knowles said she reached out of the rear window, felt something soft and warm on the roof, and found her hand covered in black dust. When the car dropped back onto the road a rear tyre burst. The family reported it at Mundrabilla. It is one of Australia’s best-known close-encounter stories.

timeline.text: A bright light is seen ahead; a glowing ball follows the car.
The object appears to settle on the roof and the car is lifted.
The car drops back onto the road and a rear tyre bursts; the family drives on and reports it at Mundrabilla.

sources.label: UFO Evidence — Knowles family encounter, Mundrabilla

records.title: Villa Urquiza Christmas sighting
records.shape: Silver object
records.witnesses: More than 7,500
records.summary: On Christmas Day 1988 a silver object crossed the Villa Urquiza neighbourhood of Buenos Aires, watched by thousands of people. The city airport reported an object heading west toward Avenida General Paz. It is often called Argentina's most spectacular UFO sighting.

timeline.text: Silver object seen over Villa Urquiza.

records.title: Voronezh park landing
records.explanation: Reported by the Soviet news agency TASS; later widely regarded as a children’s story amplified by the press.
records.shape: Large red sphere / oval
records.witnesses: Mainly children in a city park
records.summary: TASS reported that children in a Voronezh park saw a large red ball land and tall beings emerge. Soviet reporting of the case — unusual at the time — made headlines worldwide.

timeline.text: Sighting in the park.
TASS publishes the account.

records.title: Belgian UFO wave — F-16 intercepts
records.explanation: The Belgian Air Force report left the radar contacts unexplained; critics attribute the F-16 lock-ons to the other fighter and to Bragg scattering. The famous Petit-Rechain triangle photo was admitted to be a hoax in 2011.
records.shape: Dark triangle with bright corner lights
records.witnesses: ~13,500 reports in the wave; gendarmes; Air Force
records.summary: Beginning with a sighting by two gendarmes at Eupen on 29 November 1989, thousands of Belgians reported large, slow triangles with lights. On the night of 30–31 March 1990, after ground and radar reports, two Belgian Air Force F-16s from Beauvechain made nine interception attempts and obtained brief radar locks; the Air Force published its report openly.

timeline.text: Gendarmes in Eupen report a lit triangle.
Lights reported near Thorembais-Gembloux; Glons radar has contacts.
Two F-16s scramble from Beauvechain.
Nine intercepts, three brief lock-ons.
Gendarmes see four lights fade and scatter.

records.title: Calvine photograph
records.explanation: The MoD never explained it; proposed explanations include a rock reflected in water and a hoax. The photographers have never been identified.
records.shape: Large diamond hovering; a Harrier jet nearby
records.witnesses: Two unidentified walkers
records.summary: Two men walking above Calvine photographed a large, silent diamond-shaped object hovering while a military jet flew past. Their negatives went from the Daily Record to the Ministry of Defence and vanished. A surviving print surfaced in 2022 and was published worldwide.

timeline.text: Six photographs taken.
MoD documents mentioning the case reach The National Archives.
Original photographic print published by David Clarke.

records.title: Montreal — lights over the Bonaventure Hotel
records.shape: Ring of 8–10 bright lights; a huge round form
records.witnesses: Hotel guests and staff, passers-by, police officers
records.summary: From 7:20 to 10:20 p.m., people on the rooftop pool deck of the Bonaventure Hotel and in the streets below watched 8 to 10 lights hanging in a circle above them, sending down bright white rays. Some described a huge round object behind the lights. Police officers attended, and the next day La Presse reported the sighting. It drifted slowly north and was never identified.

timeline.text: Lights noticed above the hotel's rooftop pool.
Crowds gather; police officers attend.
Lights drift north and fade.

records.title: Alitalia MD-80 near miss over Kent
records.explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority and the Ministry of Defence looked at missiles, weather balloons and rockets and ruled each one out, then closed the inquiry without an answer. The files were released by the National Archives in October 2008.
records.shape: Brown, missile-shaped object
records.witnesses: Capt. Achille Zaghetti, with 57 people aboard
records.summary: At about 8 p.m. on April 21, 1991, an Alitalia MD-80 flying from Milan to Heathrow with 57 people aboard was at 22,000 feet over the army ranges at Lydd, on the Kent coast, when Capt. Achille Zaghetti saw a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 feet above the airliner and shouted “Look out, look out”. The London control centre told him it had an unknown target on radar 10 nautical miles behind him. The Ministry of Defence and the Civil Aviation Authority investigated as an airmiss, ruled out a missile, a weather balloon and a rocket, and closed the case unsolved.

timeline.text: At 22,000 ft near Lydd, the captain sees a brown, missile-shaped object pass about 1,000 ft above.
Control reports an unknown radar target 10 nautical miles behind the airliner.
The MoD and CAA rule out a missile, a balloon and a rocket and close the inquiry.
The files are released by the National Archives.

sources.label: Irish Examiner — Pilot reported “missile” near miss, MoD files show (2008)
Kent Online — MoD reveals Kent X-files (2008)

records.title: Mexico City eclipse videos
records.explanation: Astronomers identified the brightest object as Venus (with Mars and Regulus nearby), made visible by the darkness of totality. Reflections in glass, camera artefacts and hoaxes account for others; not every video has been explained.
records.shape: Metallic disc or bright point, sometimes with a wavy haze
records.witnesses: Dozens of video and photo recordings by different people
records.summary: Millions in Mexico watched the total solar eclipse of July 11, 1991, with totality in Mexico City at 13:24 and lasting more than six minutes. At least 16 photographers and videographers recorded a bright, disc-like object near the Sun in the sky, some with a wavy trail of haze behind it. The sightings were widely seen on television and the case is a classic in Mexican ufology. Astronomers pointed out that the darkness of totality shows Venus, which stood a few degrees from the star Regulus, and that other planets also come into view, which fits many of the videos but not necessarily the apparent motion some of them show.

timeline.text: Totality begins in Mexico City; the sky darkens and Venus and other planets appear.
Maximum eclipse; many people film and photograph the sky.
Videos of a bright disc near the Sun are broadcast and debated; astronomers name Venus.

sources.label: Tim Printy — The July 11, 1991 Mexico City UFOs

records.title: Cosford incident
records.place: RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury, Shropshire
records.explanation: Most of the evening reports matched the re-entry of the rocket body that had launched the Russian satellite Cosmos 2238. The MoD found no threat. Nick Pope, who investigated for the MoD, argued that later reports, including a meteorological officer's at RAF Shawbury, were never explained.
records.shape: Triangular craft; lights in formation
records.witnesses: Police officers, RAF personnel, members of the public
records.summary: Over the night of March 30–31, 1993, police officers, RAF personnel and the public across England and Wales reported lights in formation and a large triangular craft. A patrol at RAF Cosford saw it pass over the base. At RAF Shawbury a meteorological officer described a huge craft moving slowly across the airfield and sweeping a light beam over the ground. The MoD's Nick Pope pressed the case internally, and the files were later released to The National Archives.

timeline.text: Reports begin across southern England and the Midlands.
Russian rocket body re-enters over the UK.
Patrol at RAF Cosford sees a craft pass over.
Meteorological officer at RAF Shawbury watches a large craft with a light beam.

sources.label: The National Archives (UK) — MoD UFO files

records.title: Air France 3532 — radar-visual over Coulommiers
records.explanation: GEIPAN, the French space agency’s UAP office, classes the case as unexplained after investigation. The military radar track is real but does not match the crew’s account closely: the crew saw a stationary object far off to the left, while the radar target was about a mile to the right and moving. Both vanished at the same moment.
records.shape: Huge brown or dark-red disc or bell that seemed to change shape
records.witnesses: Capt. Jean-Charles Duboc, First Officer Valérie Chauffour and a chief steward
records.summary: At 13:14 on January 28, 1994, the crew of Air France flight 3532, an Airbus A320 from Nice to London, was cruising at about 11,900 metres near Coulommiers, east of Paris, when the chief steward and both pilots saw a huge object, like a brown bell or disc, off to the left. It seemed to change shape, stayed in view for about a minute and then vanished abruptly. Reims air traffic control had no traffic there, but the military radar at Cinq-Mars-la-Pile recorded a track for about 50 seconds that crossed the airliner’s path and disappeared at the same moment the crew lost sight of the object. The radar return and the crew’s description do not agree on distance or side, which is part of why the case remains open.

timeline.text: The chief steward and both pilots see a large brown or dark-red object to the left.
It seems to change shape, then vanishes all at once.
Reims control has no traffic there; the crew file a report.
The Cinq-Mars-la-Pile military radar is found to have tracked an unidentified echo for 50 seconds.

points.note: The object is seen to the left

records.title: Ariel School, Ruwa
records.explanation: Skeptics suggest mass suggestion after a meteor/re-entry seen across southern Africa two days earlier; many former pupils still stand by their accounts.

records.witnesses: 62 pupils aged 5–12
records.summary: During morning break, 62 children said a silver craft landed in bush beside the playground and one or two small figures in black watched them. Their drawings were collected within days, and Harvard psychiatrist John Mack interviewed them.

timeline.text: Bright re-entry/meteor seen over southern Africa.
Children’s sighting during break.

records.title: British Airways 5061 near miss over the Pennines
records.place: About 8 nautical miles south-east of Manchester Airport
records.explanation: The Civil Aviation Authority’s Joint Airmiss Working Group could not identify the object and rated the airmiss “unassessable”. No other aircraft or balloon was found, and no radar return was seen.
records.shape: Wedge-shaped object with small white lights and a black stripe
records.witnesses: Capt. Roger Wills and First Officer Mark Stuart
records.summary: At 18:48 on January 6, 1995, British Airways flight 5061, a Boeing 737 from Milan with 60 passengers aboard, was descending through about 4,000 feet over the Pennines toward Manchester when both pilots saw a lighted object pass very close down the right side, going the other way. They described it as wedge-shaped, with small white lights and a black stripe; the first officer ducked as it went by. Nothing showed on radar. The Joint Airmiss Working Group studied the report and, unable to identify the object, called it “unassessable”.

timeline.text: Descending through 4,000 ft, heading north, both pilots see a lit object ahead.
It flashes down the right side in the opposite direction; the first officer ducks.
Manchester radar shows nothing; the crew file an airmiss report.
The Joint Airmiss Working Group rates the encounter “unassessable” (report 2/95).

points.note: The object passes down the right side

records.title: Bariloche — the blackout and Aerolíneas Argentinas 674
records.place: San Carlos de Bariloche airport, Río Negro, Argentina
records.explanation: No explanation was found. Carlos Angueira, president of a local astronomy association, rejected a meteorite or a refraction, saying such things cannot “stop in the middle of the sky”. The case drew new attention in 2026, when it appeared among the Latin American incidents in UAP files released by the Pentagon.
records.shape: A light between white and amber, like a star but much larger; later described as green and white, about 30 m across
records.witnesses: Capt. Jorge Polanco, his crew and passengers; the tower chief, Daniel García; the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne
records.summary: At about 8:15 p.m. on July 31, 1995, Aerolíneas Argentinas flight 674, a Boeing 727 from Buenos Aires under Capt. Jorge Polanco, was coming in to land at Bariloche when the airport lost power, and then the whole city went dark as the airliner neared the runway, forcing a go-around. A light “between white and amber”, like a star but much larger and brighter, then flew on a parallel course about 100 metres from the plane. When the power came back the 727 climbed to 3,000 metres, descended and landed, and the light left at full speed toward the south-east. The tower chief and the crew of a Gendarmería Cheyenne flying 600 metres higher saw it too, and the tower’s instruments swung from one direction to another for no clear reason. Interviewed in 2026, Polanco said: “It pursued us, accompanied us for 17 minutes.”

timeline.text: The airport loses power about 15 minutes before landing; the 727 holds.
The whole city goes dark as the airliner nears the runway; it goes around.
A white-amber light keeps a parallel course about 100 m away; the tower’s instruments swing.
Power returns; the 727 climbs to 3,000 m, descends and lands; the light leaves to the south-east.
The case appears among UAP files released by the Pentagon.

points.note: Descending toward Bariloche; the airport loses power
The city goes dark near the runway; go-around
Climbs to 3,000 m with the light alongside

records.title: Varginha "ET"

records.witnesses: 3 young women; later many rumours
records.summary: Three young women said they saw a strange creature crouched near a wall, with vein-like marks on its skin, three bumps on its head and eyes like "two red balls". The lights were seen again on the nights of August 31 and September 1.

records.summary: Before dawn, a store owner in Highland and then police officers in Lebanon, Summerfield, Shiloh and Dupo independently reported a large, low triangular object with bright lights moving south-west toward Scott AFB and the Mississippi.

records.place: Tinley Park and Oak Forest, Illinois
records.explanation: Commonly attributed to balloons or kites carrying lights or flares, which match the slow drift and the colour. No one has come forward, and the cause has not been confirmed.

records.witnesses: Hundreds in the south suburbs of Chicago
records.summary: On the evening of August 21, 2004, hundreds of people in Chicago's south suburbs watched three large red lights in a triangle drift slowly and silently across the sky. They are a prominent "black triangle" style case with plenty of video.

records.title: USS Nimitz "Tic Tac"
records.place: Pacific Ocean ~100 mi SW of San Diego
records.explanation: The Pentagon released the FLIR1 video in 2020 and describes the object as unidentified. Skeptics argue the FLIR clip shows a distant aircraft; the pilots’ visual account is independent of the video.
records.shape: White, smooth 40-ft "Tic Tac"
records.witnesses: 4 aircrew (Fravor, Dietrich + WSOs), USS Princeton radar operators
records.summary: For days the cruiser USS Princeton’s SPY-1 radar tracked objects appearing at about 80,000 ft, dropping rapidly toward the sea and hovering. On 14 November, Cdr. David Fravor and Lt. records.summary: A ramp worker pushing back United Flight 446 saw a dark disc hovering low over Gate C-17; pilots, supervisors and mechanics came out to watch. records.witnesses: Aurigny captain Ray Bowyer, passengers, a second pilot

records.summary: Dozens of people around Stephenville, including a private pilot and a local constable, reported a very large, silent object with bright lights followed by fighter jets. FOIA radar records later analysed by MUFON showed unidentified returns in the area.

records.title: Morristown lights (admitted hoax)
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: Hoax. Joe Rudy and Chris Russo tied road flares to helium balloons and released them on five nights, then revealed it on April 1, 2009 with video of the launches. They were fined for disorderly conduct.

records.shape: Blue beam with an expanding white spiral
records.witnesses: Thousands across northern Norway and Sweden
records.summary: Before sunrise on December 9, 2009, people across northern Norway saw a blue-white light rise from behind the mountains, stop, and begin to spin. A glowing spiral grew outward and dissolved into a black hole-like disc. Photos and video went worldwide within hours. Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell quickly suggested a failed Russian missile, and Moscow confirmed a Bulava test failure.

records.title: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR video
records.place: Coast between San Antonio and Quinteros, Chile
records.explanation: Chile’s aerial-phenomena office (CEFAA) left the case open because it could not be certain of the object’s nature. Later analyses by sceptics proposed an aircraft’s contrail and exhaust seen by infrared as the likely cause.
records.shape: Flat, elongated object with two hot discharges
records.witnesses: Navy helicopter crew (pilot and camera operator)
records.summary: On November 11, 2014 a Chilean Navy helicopter on coastal patrol west of Santiago, at about 4,500 feet, picked up an unknown object on its high-definition infrared camera. The two-man crew also saw it with the naked eye for more than ten minutes. The captain described a flat, elongated object with two thermal discharges that did not line up with its direction of travel, and the video shows what looks like a chemical plume. The Navy’s aerial-phenomena office CEFAA examined it and later released the footage, saying it could not be sure what it was. Sceptics later said the images match the contrail of a distant aircraft.

records.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt — Gimbal & GoFast
records.place: Atlantic warning areas off Jacksonville, Florida
records.explanation: Both videos were officially released and remain "unidentified" per DoD. Analysts such as Mick West argue GoFast shows a slow object (e.g. a balloon) at ~13,000 ft that only looks fast and low because of parallax, and that Gimbal’s rotation is a glare artifact of the ATFLIR pod. AARO later published a case resolution for GoFast worked out from the sensor’s geometry and the winds aloft.
records.shape: Rotating lozenge (Gimbal); small fast object (GoFast)
records.witnesses: VFA-11 aircrew; Lt. Ryan Graves’ squadron reported near-daily objects

records.summary: In 2014–2015 F/A-18F crews of the Roosevelt strike group reported frequent unknown objects on their upgraded APG-79 radars off the East Coast. Two ATFLIR clips — "Gimbal", with a crew member exclaiming about "a whole fleet of them", and "GoFast", a small object skimming over the ocean — were released by the Pentagon in April 2020.

records.title: Ireland — airline pilots report fast lights
records.explanation: One pilot suggested a meteor or an object in re-entry, and an astronomer at the Armagh Observatory said the lights were most likely meteors. Air traffic control saw nothing on radar and no military exercises were running, so nothing has been confirmed.
records.shape: Very bright lights moving at high speed
records.witnesses: Crews of a British Airways and a Virgin Atlantic flight, and others
records.summary: At about 6:47 on the morning of November 9, 2018 the pilot of a British Airways flight from Montreal to London radioed Shannon air traffic control to ask whether military exercises were under way. A “very bright light” had come up on the left of the aircraft and “rapidly veered to the north”, then disappeared at very high speed. The crew of a Virgin Atlantic flight reported two bright lights that banked to the right and climbed away at what the pilot called “astronomical” speed, “like Mach 2”. Controllers saw nothing on radar, and no military exercises were taking place. The Irish Aviation Authority said it would investigate by confidentially interviewing the pilots. More than one crew reported it, and the story was carried by news outlets around the world.

The Irish Aviation Authority confirms it will interview the pilots; an astronomer suggests meteors.

records.title: USS Omaha sphere & USS Russell "pyramids"
records.explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the leaked clips were taken by Navy personnel. Analysts attribute the "pyramids" to the triangular aperture of a night-vision lens (bokeh) on aircraft/stars, and the Omaha sphere to a distant aircraft or balloon.
records.shape: Spherical object descending into the sea; flashing pyramid shapes
records.witnesses: Crew of USS Omaha, USS Russell and other ships
records.summary: During July 2019, several Navy ships off Southern California reported drone-like objects around them at night. A CIC video from USS Omaha shows a sphere flying over the ocean and apparently descending into the water; night-vision footage from USS Russell shows blinking pyramid-shaped lights. Both leaked in 2021 and were confirmed as authentic Navy footage.

records.title: Colorado and Nebraska drone swarms
records.place: Phillips County and the plains of north-eastern Colorado
records.explanation: State and federal agencies found that most reports were planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones, and the Colorado Department of Public Safety stood its effort down in January 2020. The large, grid-flying drones of the first reports were never tied to an operator.
records.shape: Drones with a wingspan of about 6 ft and blinking lights, in groups of six to ten, flying grid patterns
records.witnesses: Ranchers, residents and county sheriff’s deputies
records.summary: In December 2019, residents and deputies in north-eastern Colorado and western Nebraska began reporting drones with wingspans of about six feet flying in groups of six to ten, at 200 to 500 feet, in grid patterns across the plains, mostly between about 7 and 10 p.m.; one witness counted 19. County sheriffs asked the public for information, and more than 70 local, state and federal agencies met in Brush on January 6, 2020. The FAA said no drone company or test site had authorized flights there, and the Air Force, which had run counter-drone exercises at F. E. Warren AFB, would neither claim nor deny the drones. As the sightings spread, more and more turned out to be planets, stars and airliners, and the state ended its search later that month.

timeline.text: Reports of large drones flying grid patterns at night begin in north-eastern Colorado.
Sheriffs ask the public for information; the FAA finds no authorized drone flights there.
The Air Force neither claims nor denies the drones.
More than 70 agencies meet in Brush to coordinate.
Searches find mostly planets, stars, aircraft and hobby drones; the state stands down.

records.title: American Airlines 2292 — “cruise-missile type of thing”
records.place: Northeastern New Mexico, at about 36,000 ft
records.explanation: No explanation has been given. The FAA said air traffic controllers saw no object on their radar. The Pentagon said the military was not conducting tests in the area that day, and the FBI said it was aware of the report.
records.shape: Long cylinder, “almost like a cruise missile”
records.witnesses: The crew of American Airlines Flight 2292
records.summary: On February 21, 2021, at about 12:29 p.m. local time, the crew of American Airlines Flight 2292, an Airbus A320 flying from Cincinnati to Phoenix at about 36,000 feet over the north-east corner of New Mexico, radioed: “Do you have any targets up here? We just had something go right over the top of us. I hate to say this, but it looked like a long cylindrical object that almost looked like a cruise missile type of thing, moving really fast right over the top of us.” The transmission was recorded by Steve Douglass, a radio listener. American Airlines at first denied that it was authentic, then confirmed that it was from Flight 2292 after talking to the crew. The FAA said controllers saw nothing on radar, and the Pentagon said it had no tests in the area.

records.title: Chinese surveillance balloon
records.explanation: A PRC high-altitude surveillance balloon; shot down by an F-22 AIM-9X off Surfside Beach, South Carolina, and recovered by the U.S. Navy.

records.witnesses: Millions; NORAD tracking

records.title: February 2023 shoot-downs (Alaska, Yukon, Lake Huron)
records.explanation: The White House said the three objects were most likely benign commercial or research balloons; none was recovered. An infrared video of the Lake Huron shoot-down was released in 2026 as DOW-UAP-PR071.

records.title: Langley Air Force Base drone incursions
records.explanation: The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024 and said the drones did not appear to show hostile intent, but neither it nor NORAD has said who flew them.
records.shape: Drones of several sizes; the first reportedly about 20 ft long
records.witnesses: Base personnel and U.S. military officials
records.summary: From the evening of December 6, 2023, unauthorized drones flew over Langley Air Force Base, home of F-22 Raptor squadrons, across Hampton Roads from the Navy’s largest base at Norfolk, on and off for 17 days. The Wall Street Journal later reported that they typically arrived 45 minutes to an hour after sunset, that the first was about 20 feet long and flew at 3,000 to 4,000 feet, and that a dozen or more smaller drones followed. The Pentagon confirmed the incursions in October 2024. Gen. Glen VanHerck, who led NORAD at the time, later said the military had warned for years that it was not ready for this threat; he gave no new details about who was operating the drones.

timeline.text: The first drones appear over Langley, 45 minutes to an hour after sunset.

records.title: New Jersey drone sightings
records.place: Morris County, New Jersey, and the Northeast
records.statusLabel: Mundane explanation widely accepted or officially assessed
records.explanation: A joint FBI, DHS, FAA and DoD review found a mix of lawful commercial, hobbyist and law-enforcement drones, crewed aircraft and stars, with no threat to national security. In January 2025 the White House said the drones over New Jersey had been authorized by the FAA for research and other purposes.
records.shape: Large lighted drones; many reports were aircraft
records.witnesses: Thousands of residents, police, state officials
records.summary: From mid-November 2024, residents in Morris County reported large, lighted drones flying at night, including over Picatinny Arsenal and near the president-elect's golf club in Bedminster. Reports spread across New Jersey and into New York, Pennsylvania and beyond. The FAA placed temporary flight restrictions over dozens of sites. Stewart International Airport briefly closed its runways, and many viral videos turned out to show airliners.

records.title: Drones over the U.S. air bases in England
records.place: RAF Lakenheath, Mildenhall, Feltwell and Fairford, England
records.explanation: The U.S. Air Force and the Ministry of Defence confirmed the drones, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an investigation, but the operators were not identified.
records.shape: Small drones of varying number and type
records.witnesses: U.S. Air Force personnel; residents of nearby villages
records.summary: Between November 20 and 26, 2024, small drones were seen over and around four bases in England used by the U.S. Air Force: RAF Lakenheath, home of the 48th Fighter Wing, RAF Mildenhall, RAF Feltwell and RAF Fairford. The Air Force said “small unmanned aerial systems were spotted in the vicinity of and over RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall and RAF Feltwell between 20 and 22 November”. Air traffic into Mildenhall was disrupted: on November 21 a KC-46 tanker that had brought F-35s across the Atlantic turned back and diverted to Prestwick. British troops with counter-drone equipment were sent to help, and the Ministry of Defence Police opened an inquiry. Similar reports came from U.S. bases in Germany that December.

timeline.text: Drones are reported over and near Lakenheath, Mildenhall and Feltwell.
A KC-46 tanker bound for Mildenhall diverts to Prestwick because of drone reports.
More incursions, including at Fairford; British counter-drone teams are deployed.
The Ministry of Defence Police open an investigation; the operators remain unknown.
